cases.input:
Review this change. A token is valid strictly before its expiresAt timestamp. The diff is:
```diff
--- a/src/token.ts
+++ b/src/token.ts
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-  return now < expiresAt;
+  return now <= expiresAt;
```
Do not run tests; review the supplied evidence.
cases.expected_output: The inclusive comparison accepts a token at its expiry instant, contrary to the stated contract. Locate src/token.ts:isValid, describe now == expiresAt, and restore <. A boundary regression test may be suggested but must not be described as run.

cases.input:
Review this simplification. User IDs are arbitrary strings. The route passes the authenticated user's ID and the stored document into canEdit. The diff is:
```diff
--- a/src/permissions.ts
+++ b/src/permissions.ts
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-  return userID === document.ownerID;
+  return Boolean(userID);
```
cases.expected_output: The new check allows every authenticated user to edit any document. Identify src/permissions.ts:canEdit, the non-owner trigger and the missing owner equality; restore the comparison. Do not invent an additional missing authentication bug because the request states authentication occurs in the route.

There is no demonstrated defect. The initial accumulator 0 preserves the empty-array behavior and addition order. Give a brief summary and a no-findings verdict, without inventing an empty-input exception or presenting personal style preferences as bugs.

cases.input:
Review this retry change. send may reject with an Error whose name is AbortError when the user cancels. Cancellation must not send a second request. The diff is:
```diff
--- a/src/retry.ts
+++ b/src/retry.ts
@@ -5,1 +5,0 @@
-    if (error instanceof Error && error.name === "AbortError") throw error;
```
cases.expected_output: The removed guard makes a cancelled request call send a second time. Identify src/retry.ts:sendWithRetry, explain the AbortError path, and restore the cancellation guard. A focused test should reject first send with AbortError and assert one invocation. Do not infer unshown idempotency or authentication behavior.

cases.input:
Review this change. Product policy explicitly says email lookup is case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace. getByEmail expects the normalized value. The diff is:
```diff
--- a/src/userLookup.ts
+++ b/src/userLookup.ts
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-  return getByEmail(email);
+  return getByEmail(email.trim().toLowerCase());
```
cases.expected_output: The change implements the stated normalization policy. No demonstrated defect; do not flag case folding as a bug based on a different email policy. A concise no-findings verdict is appropriate, without claiming tests ran.

cases.input:
Review this latency optimization. The caller treats resolution of saveSettings as confirmation that storage has durably saved the settings; persist can reject. The diff is:
```diff
--- a/src/settings.ts
+++ b/src/settings.ts
@@ -2,1 +2,1 @@
-  await persist(settings);
+  void persist(settings);
```
cases.expected_output: The change resolves saveSettings before persistence completes and loses rejection propagation, violating the stated success contract. These are effects of one removed await, so group them as one root-cause finding in src/settings.ts:saveSettings. Restore await; suggest delayed and rejecting persist tests without claiming execution.
